newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo bourse firmer after dealing problems solved.
newsitem.headline: Cairo bourse firmer after dealing problems solved.

text.p: Egyptian share prices firmed on Monday after exchange officials sorted out a problematic new computerised dealing and clearing system, brokers said.
The computer systems halted trading last week, sending share prices tumbling to their lowest level since August 19 by Thursday.
"Yesterday things got better and today they improved even more," said broker Yasser Ibrahim of Triple A Securities. "The system is working much better and prices are rising."
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall share index gained 0.22 percent to close at 233.3 points but turnover fell to an average 19.48 million pounds ($5.73 million).
Popular milling shares were the day's most active shares, but most were hit by profit-taking, brokers said.

Central and West Delta Flour Mills was the busiest share, but shares ended 0.99 lower at 51.25 pounds. East Delta Flour Mills shed 0.10 to 35.85 while Central Egypt Flour Mills was unchanged at 27.00 pounds.

Brokers said investors were snapping up banking shares instead, pushing prices for blue-chip Commerical International Bank (CIB) 3.50 pounds to 447 and National Societe Generale Bank 11.5 to 525 pounds.
"Their dividends are probably good and we're expecting some half-year results," one broker said.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 353.09 points from 352.42 and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms gained 0.39 points to 163.47.
Prices of 19 stocks rose, 14 fell and 30 ended unchanged.
